sections.skill: Build a direct argument about even, odd and multiples from definitions

questions.prompt: Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. Put the steps of a direct proof that the sum of two odd integers is even in order.

items.text: Let m = 2a + 1 and n = 2b + 1, where a and b are integers.
Since a + b + 1 is an integer, m + n is even.

questions.correct_answer: Let m = 2a + 1 and n = 2b + 1, where a and b are integers. → Then m + n = 2a + 2b + 2. → So m + n = 2(a + b + 1). → Since a + b + 1 is an integer, m + n is even.

questions.prompt: Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. Which first line correctly begins a direct proof that the product of any two odd integers is odd?

choices.text: Let m = 2a + 1 and n = 2a + 1, where a is an integer.
Let m = 2a + 1 and n = 2b + 1, where a and b are integers.
Assume that m times n is odd.

questions.correct_answer: Let m = 2a + 1 and n = 2b + 1, where a and b are integers.

questions.prompt: Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. A proof that an even integer plus an odd integer is odd reaches the line m + n = 2a + 2b + 1. Which line correctly finishes it?

choices.text: Since 4 + 3 = 7 is odd, m + n is odd.
m + n is odd because the expression 2a + 2b + 1 contains a 1.
m + n = 2(a + b + 1), so m + n is even.
m + n = 2(a + b) + 1, and a + b is an integer, so m + n is odd.

questions.correct_answer: m + n = 2(a + b) + 1, and a + b is an integer, so m + n is odd.

Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. To show that 6n + 4 is even for every integer n, write 6n + 4 = 2(pn + q). Give the numbers p and q.
questions.rule: (p == 3 and q == 2) and isInteger(p) and isInteger(q)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (p == 3 and q == 2) and isInteger(p) and isInteger(q) (example: p = 3, q = 2)

sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. Put the steps of a direct proof that if n is a multiple of 3, then n squared is a multiple of 9 in a correct order. (Two orders are correct.)

items.text: Let n = 3k, where k is an integer.
k squared is an integer, because k is an integer.
So n squared is 9 times an integer, a multiple of 9.

questions.correct_answer: Let n = 3k, where k is an integer. → Then n squared = 9k squared. → k squared is an integer, because k is an integer. → So n squared is 9 times an integer, a multiple of 9.

questions.prompt: Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. Which is a correct direct proof that the sum of three consecutive integers is a multiple of 3?

choices.text: n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1), and n + 1 is an integer.
n + n + n = 3n, which is a multiple of 3.

questions.correct_answer: n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1), and n + 1 is an integer.

questions.prompt: Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. Put the steps of a direct proof that the square of an odd integer leaves remainder 1 when divided by 4 in order.

items.text: Let n = 2k + 1, where k is an integer.
Since k squared + k is an integer, n squared leaves remainder 1 when divided by 4.

questions.correct_answer: Let n = 2k + 1, where k is an integer. → Then n squared = 4k squared + 4k + 1. → So n squared = 4(k squared + k) + 1. → Since k squared + k is an integer, n squared leaves remainder 1 when divided by 4.

questions.correct_answer: It uses the same k for both, so it only covers the case m = n.
